PA.name: Product Analyst
PA.summary: Understand product behavior, measure journeys, and recommend changes with clear evidence.
PA.scenario_A: A consumer app's downloads are stable, but weekly active users are down 15% for a month. Synthetic case; no real company is implicated.

questions_A.prompt: What would you clarify before investigating the 15% decline?
questions_A.ideal: Metric definition, dates, segment, instrumentation, seasonality

questions_A.prompt: Which usage funnel or cohorts would you examine first?
questions_A.ideal: Acquisition→activation→repeat use; weekly cohorts; denominators

questions_A.prompt: Downloads are stable but first-week activation fell. Give three hypotheses and how you'd distinguish them.
questions_A.ideal: UX regression, mix shift, tracking issue; evidence per hypothesis

questions_A.prompt: You can investigate only one hypothesis today. Which and why?
questions_A.ideal: Prioritization using impact, evidence and effort; check data validity

questions_A.prompt: What would you measure after a fix, and what guardrail would you monitor?
questions_A.ideal: Activation and retained use; clear windows/guardrail

PA.scenario_B: Signup-to-verification conversion has declined on Android, but iOS has remained stable. The event instrumentation recently changed.

questions_B.prompt: Before diagnosing verification conversion, what definitions and baseline would you confirm?
questions_B.ideal: Metric definition, dates, segment, instrumentation, seasonality

questions_B.prompt: Which stages and cohorts of the verification journey would you compare?
questions_B.ideal: Acquisition→activation→repeat use; weekly cohorts; denominators

questions_B.prompt: Offer three possible explanations for the Android decline and explain what data distinguishes them.
questions_B.ideal: UX regression, mix shift, tracking issue; evidence per hypothesis

questions_B.prompt: Which explanation would you investigate first, and why?
questions_B.ideal: Prioritization using impact, evidence and effort; check data validity

questions_B.prompt: What success and guardrail metrics would you use after a change?
questions_B.ideal: Activation and retained use; clear windows/guardrail

APM.name: Associate Product Manager
APM.summary: Discover user needs, prioritize product decisions, and coordinate measurable delivery.
APM.scenario_A: A team has capacity to ship only one improvement in the next cycle: onboarding simplification, smarter notifications or a new recommendation feature.

questions_A.prompt: What outcome and user group must be clarified before choosing?
questions_A.ideal: Customer need, baseline outcome, constraints

questions_A.prompt: What evidence would you collect about the three opportunities?
questions_A.ideal: User research, funnel issues, costs, complaints

questions_A.prompt: Choose one feature using explicit criteria and defend the trade-off.
questions_A.ideal: User impact, confidence, effort, risk, alternatives

questions_A.prompt: What is the smallest testable version and how would you describe it to engineering?
questions_A.ideal: MVP scope, user story, acceptance conditions

questions_A.prompt: What outcome metric and guardrails would decide whether to continue?
questions_A.ideal: Clear metric tree, experiment and risk constraints

APM.scenario_B: A job platform can build only one next-quarter feature: simplify applications, improve search filters, or add recruiter messaging.

questions_B.prompt: What user group and outcome would you clarify before choosing a feature?
questions_B.ideal: Customer need, baseline outcome, constraints

questions_B.prompt: What research or metrics would you gather for the three options?
questions_B.ideal: User research, funnel issues, costs, complaints

questions_B.prompt: Pick one feature and justify the trade-off with an explicit decision framework.
questions_B.ideal: User impact, confidence, effort, risk, alternatives

questions_B.prompt: Define the smallest usable version and its acceptance criteria.
questions_B.ideal: MVP scope, user story, acceptance conditions

questions_B.prompt: What would indicate success and what unintended effects would you monitor?
questions_B.ideal: Clear metric tree, experiment and risk constraints

PO.name: Product Operations Associate
PO.summary: Keep product launches and operating processes running reliably across teams.
PO.scenario_A: A digital onboarding process takes 30% longer this month even though application volume is stable.

questions_A.prompt: What would you clarify about turnaround time and the affected users?
questions_A.ideal: Mean/median, SLA, segments, measurement window

questions_A.prompt: Map the stages, owners and possible queues.
questions_A.ideal: Queue time vs touch time, rework, handoffs

questions_A.prompt: How would you separate a product defect from a staffing or process bottleneck?
questions_A.ideal: Logs, queue aging, errors, capacity measures

questions_A.prompt: Pick a short-term containment and a longer-term change. Explain the trade-off.
questions_A.ideal: Escalation, prioritization, owner, root-cause remediation

questions_A.prompt: What launch/QA and operational monitoring would prevent recurrence?
questions_A.ideal: SLA dashboard, alerts, UAT, post-fix checks

PO.scenario_B: After a new feature launch, support tickets spike and resolutions slow down despite unchanged staffing.

questions_B.prompt: What definitions, customer segments and time windows would you clarify?
questions_B.ideal: Mean/median, SLA, segments, measurement window

questions_B.prompt: Map the support process and identify where tickets may be accumulating.
questions_B.ideal: Queue time vs touch time, rework, handoffs

questions_B.prompt: How would you distinguish product defects from operations capacity or process issues?
questions_B.ideal: Logs, queue aging, errors, capacity measures

questions_B.prompt: What immediate response and longer-term fix would you prioritize?
questions_B.ideal: Escalation, prioritization, owner, root-cause remediation

questions_B.prompt: What monitoring and release quality controls would prevent recurrence?
questions_B.ideal: SLA dashboard, alerts, UAT, post-fix checks

DA.name: Data Analyst
DA.summary: Prepare and analyze data, check its quality, and communicate reliable business findings.
DA.scenario_A: A signup dashboard shows 1,000 signups and 450 activated users this month, versus 800 signups and 400 activated last month. The new tracking event was introduced midmonth.

questions_A.prompt: Calculate activation rates for both months and interpret the change.
questions_A.ideal: 50%→45%; rates down 5 pp despite count up

questions_A.prompt: What data-definition problems could make this comparison invalid?
questions_A.ideal: Event change, unique IDs, eligibility, cutoff

questions_A.prompt: What checks would you run before publishing the dashboard?
questions_A.ideal: Duplicates, missingness, join grain, window consistency

questions_A.prompt: Which two segments would you compare first?
questions_A.ideal: New/returning, platform, source, region; rationale

questions_A.prompt: How would you communicate this cautiously to management?
questions_A.ideal: Caveat, magnitude, next checks, no false causation

DA.scenario_B: Purchases have increased after a pricing change, but revenue per active customer has declined.

questions_B.prompt: What metrics would you calculate and how would you interpret their movement?
questions_B.ideal: 50%→45%; rates down 5 pp despite count up

questions_B.prompt: What definitions, joins and recording changes could distort this conclusion?
questions_B.ideal: Event change, unique IDs, eligibility, cutoff

questions_B.prompt: Which validity checks would you run before publishing the result?
questions_B.ideal: Duplicates, missingness, join grain, window consistency

questions_B.prompt: What customer segments or periods would you compare first?
questions_B.ideal: New/returning, platform, source, region; rationale

questions_B.prompt: How would you explain the trade-offs and uncertainty to management?
questions_B.ideal: Caveat, magnitude, next checks, no false causation

BA.name: Business Analyst
BA.summary: Turn business problems and stakeholder needs into clear requirements and measurable solutions.
BA.scenario_A: A company wants to replace spreadsheet-based leave approvals with a self-service workflow, but HR and line managers disagree on exception policies.

questions_A.prompt: Who are your stakeholders and what outcomes do you clarify?
questions_A.ideal: Employees, HR, managers, payroll, audit, outcomes

questions_A.prompt: How would you document the current process and pain points?
questions_A.ideal: Current-state steps, turnaround, error/exception rates

questions_A.prompt: How would you resolve conflicting approval rules?
questions_A.ideal: Decision rights, exceptions, escalation, policy owner

questions_A.prompt: State three testable requirements or acceptance criteria.
questions_A.ideal: Role permissions, SLA, audit trail, edge cases

questions_A.prompt: What would you evaluate after rollout?
questions_A.ideal: Adoption, SLA, errors, auditability, employee feedback

BA.scenario_B: Finance, risk, and customer support disagree on the rules for a new self-service refund workflow.

questions_B.prompt: Identify the relevant stakeholders and the desired business outcomes.
questions_B.ideal: Employees, HR, managers, payroll, audit, outcomes

questions_B.prompt: How would you capture the current-state refund process and issues?
questions_B.ideal: Current-state steps, turnaround, error/exception rates

questions_B.prompt: How would you resolve the conflicting approval and exception rules?
questions_B.ideal: Decision rights, exceptions, escalation, policy owner

questions_B.prompt: Write three testable requirements or acceptance conditions.
questions_B.ideal: Role permissions, SLA, audit trail, edge cases

questions_B.prompt: How would you evaluate the solution after rollout?
questions_B.ideal: Adoption, SLA, errors, auditability, employee feedback

PMM.name: Product Marketing Associate
PMM.summary: Research customers, position products, and design measurable go-to-market plans.

resource.title: Product Marketing Alliance: PMM interview guide

PMM.scenario_A: A B2B analytics tool launches a simplified dashboard for small retail chains but adoption is low.

questions_A.prompt: Who is the highest-priority buyer/user and what job do they need done?
questions_A.ideal: Decision maker, user, pain, segment selection

questions_A.prompt: What positioning statement would differentiate the offer?
questions_A.ideal: Target, pain, value, proof, distinction

questions_A.prompt: Which two channels would you test first with limited budget?
questions_A.ideal: Channel logic, reach, buying journey, resources

questions_A.prompt: What would sales/customer-success need to explain the launch?
questions_A.ideal: Messaging, objections, demo, enablement

questions_A.prompt: How would you measure launch success and separate awareness from activation?
questions_A.ideal: Funnel, conversion, adoption, feedback loops

PMM.scenario_B: An existing learning app is launching a paid employer offering, but its users are currently students.

questions_B.prompt: Who are the new buyers, users, and stakeholders, and what jobs are they hiring the product for?
questions_B.ideal: Decision maker, user, pain, segment selection

questions_B.prompt: Write a differentiated positioning statement for the new offer.
questions_B.ideal: Target, pain, value, proof, distinction

questions_B.prompt: Which two GTM channels would you test first with limited resources?
questions_B.ideal: Channel logic, reach, buying journey, resources

questions_B.prompt: What sales-enablement materials and objections should the launch plan address?
questions_B.ideal: Messaging, objections, demo, enablement

questions_B.prompt: How would you distinguish campaign awareness from actual adoption and willingness to pay?
questions_B.ideal: Funnel, conversion, adoption, feedback loops
